input.summary: Fix illusory cap basis in § 21.1: all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement (not the USD 12,000 "Fees" under the first Order Form), with a USD 1,000,000 floor.
input.comment: [Playbook] As drafted the mutual cap is illusory: "Fees" is defined as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so Vendor's exposure is a fraction of contract value. We tie the cap to all amounts paid or payable by Customer in the preceding twelve months with a USD 1,000,000 floor; indemnification, confidentiality, data-protection and security claims remain outside the cap as Excluded Claims. If the floor is not acceptable, we can fall back to twelve months' total amounts payable.

input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
input.rationale: The cap is mutual and the carve-outs in § 21.3 (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) plus the payment-obligation exclusion match the playbook. However the cap basis is illusory: "Fees" is defined in § 1.5/1.6 as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee stated in the first Order Form, and § 21.1 further narrows the basis to the first Order Form only, so Vendor's aggregate exposure is capped near USD 12,000 regardless of subscription spend. There is also no USD 1,000,000 floor. Redline ties the cap to all amounts paid or payable by Customer under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months, with a USD 1,000,000 floor, leaving the existing mutuality and Excluded Claims structure intact.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 20 of the MSA already reaches our preferred playbook position on vendor indemnification:

| Playbook requirement | Where satisfied |
|---|---|
| Vendor IP infringement indemnity for Services/Deliverables | 20.1 — unqualified, no modification/combination exclusions |
| Extends to Customer affiliates | 20.1 — Customer, Affiliates, directors, officers, employees, agents (Affiliate broadly defined at 1.1) |
| Vendor breach of law | 20.2 |
| Data breach caused by Vendor | 20.2 — unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data |
| Gross negligence / wilful misconduct | 20.2 — plus fraud and bodily injury/property damage (better than model) |
| Standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation) | 20.4 — material-prejudice qualifier on notice, cooperation at indemnitor's expense, no prejudicial settlement without consent |
| Customer indemnity stays narrow | 20.3 — only unmodified Customer material used strictly as authorised and Customer's own breach of law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications, combinations, Vendor instructions |

Two additional points worth noting in our favour:

- **20.5** gives the procure/modify/replace/refund remedies but expressly says they are *in addition to* Vendor's defence obligation, and bars Vendor from terminating unaffected Services. This is why we land at preferred rather than the fallback — the remedies are not a substitute for the indemnity.
- **21.3** confirms indemnification obligations, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, and IP infringement are all "Excluded Claims" sitting outside the mutual cap in 21.1, so the fallback's 3× annual fees super-cap is unnecessary.

One item outside this rule's scope that a liability-focused review should pick up: the cap in **21.1** is measured against fees "under the **first Order Form**" rather than all fees paid under the Agreement, which could understate our recovery in a multi-order relationship. That does not affect indemnity claims (they are Excluded Claims), so I have left it for the limitation-of-liability rule.

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 20 already delivers the preferred position. Clause 20.1 gives an unqualified Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Services or Deliverables, extended to Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel (Affiliate is broadly defined at 1.1). Clause 20.2 adds the required misconduct limbs: Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud — matching, and in the case of fraud and bodily injury exceeding, our model language. Clause 20.4 sets out standard procedure (prompt notice with a material-prejudice qualifier, cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, control of defence, and no prejudicial settlement without consent). Clause 20.5 provides the procure/modify/replace/refund remedies for infringement claims and, helpfully, states they are in addition to (not in lieu of) the defence obligation and bars termination of unaffected Services.

Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 is appropriately narrow: limited to unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised, and Customer's violation of Applicable Law in its authorised use, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications, combinations and Vendor instructions. Vendor's IP indemnity carries no Customer-modification/combination exclusions, so we sit at the preferred rather than the fallback position, and no 3× super-cap is needed. Clause 21.3 further confirms that indemnification obligations, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud and IP infringement are Excluded Claims and therefore sit outside the mutual liability cap in 21.1. No edit required for this rule.

Original paragraphs:
p0083: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
p0084: 20.2 Vendor shall also defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the Customer indemnified parties from third-party claims to the extent arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; bodily injury, death, or tangible property damage caused by Vendor; unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.
p0085: 20.3 Customer shall defend and indemnify Vendor from a third-party claim alleging that unmodified Customer material supplied by Customer and used by Vendor strictly as authorized infringes an intellectual property right, or arising from Customer's violation of Applicable Law in its authorized use of the Services. Customer has no obligation to the extent a claim arises from Vendor Technology, modification, combination, or instructions.
p0086: 20.4 The indemnified Party shall give prompt notice, reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, and control of the defence, except delay excuses obligations only to the extent of material prejudice. The indemnifying Party may not settle a claim by admitting fault of, imposing non-monetary obligations on, or failing to fully release the indemnified Party without prior written consent.
p0087: 20.5 For an infringement claim, Vendor shall, at its expense and in addition to its defence obligations, procure continued use, modify or replace the affected item without materially reducing functionality, or, if neither is commercially reasonable, terminate the item and refund prepaid and implementation Fees on a straight-line three-year basis. Vendor may not terminate unaffected Services.
p0091: 21.3 “Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Northwind Analytics, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Brightline Cloud Services Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.

Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Affiliate: 1.1 “Affiliate” means, with respect to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Party. “Control” means ownership of more than fifty percent of the voting interests of an entity or the power to direct its management. An entity is an Affiliate only while that relationship continues.
Applicable Law: 1.2 “Applicable Law” means every statute, regulation, binding regulatory requirement, court order, and governmental rule applicable to a Party's performance under this Agreement, including laws concerning privacy, information security, export controls, employment, anti-bribery, and accessibility. Applicable Law does not include a private standard unless an Order Form expressly adopts it.
Customer Data: 1.3 “Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.
Deliverable: 1.4 “Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.
Fees: 1.5 “Fees” means the Implementation Fee.
Implementation Fee: 1.6 “Implementation Fee” means the one-time implementation charge of USD 12,000 stated in the first Order Form.
Services: 1.8 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

Vendor Technology does not include Customer Data or intellectual property owned by Customer before the Effective Date.
Excluded Claims: 21.3 “Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

paragraphs.text: 8. TERM AND RENEWAL

8.1 This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.

8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.

8.3 On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.
7. FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.

7.2 Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

7.3 Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

7.4 Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

7.5 Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.
7.6 Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.

7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.

**Finding: deviation (critical) — § 21.1 cap basis is illusory.**

What the document gets right: the cap is expressly mutual, § 21.2 mutually excludes indirect/consequential damages (and helpfully treats data-restoration, replacement services, notice and incident-response costs as direct damages), and § 21.3 carves out confidentiality, data-protection, security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement as uncapped Excluded Claims, with Customer's payment obligation excluded from "damages."

The defect is quantum. "Fees" is defined at § 1.5 as *only* the Implementation Fee, which § 1.6 fixes at a one-time USD 12,000 under the first Order Form — and § 21.1 compounds this by limiting the basis to the first Order Form. Vendor's total exposure is therefore capped around USD 12,000 no matter the subscription spend, well below the walk-away threshold of six months' fees.

Redline (validated, preferred level) amends only the cap sentence to the greater of (a) all amounts paid or payable by Customer under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months and (b) USD 1,000,000, preserving the existing mutuality and Excluded Claims architecture.

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The cap is mutual and the carve-outs in § 21.3 (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) plus the payment-obligation exclusion match the playbook. However the cap basis is illusory: "Fees" is defined in § 1.5/1.6 as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee stated in the first Order Form, and § 21.1 further narrows the basis to the first Order Form only, so Vendor's aggregate exposure is capped near USD 12,000 regardless of subscription spend. There is also no USD 1,000,000 floor. Redline ties the cap to all amounts paid or payable by Customer under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months, with a USD 1,000,000 floor, leaving the existing mutuality and Excluded Claims structure intact.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.quote: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: No non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binds Customer anywhere in the Agreement: searches for "solicit", "induce", "recruit", "hire", "employ" and full review of § 12 (Customer Responsibilities), § 16 (Confidentiality) and § 30 (General) return no such restriction, and there is no restricted-period language (no "twelve (12) months" or "directly or indirectly" covenant). Section 12.3 affirmatively confirms the point in our favour, preserving Customer's freedom to hire any person responding to general recruitment (an express general-solicitation carve-out) and recording that Customer has made no no-hire commitment. This is our preferred position ("no non-solicit on Customer"), so no redline is proposed. The deterministic checks on duration (≤ 12 months) and a general-solicitation carve-out are inapplicable because there is no non-solicit clause to measure; the fallback (mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire) becomes relevant only if Vendor later proposes adding one.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.

"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

paragraphs.text: 24. ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL

24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.

24.2 Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld for an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.

24.3 For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.

24.4 Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall cooperate with reasonable administrative changes needed to reflect a permitted successor.
30. GENERAL

30.1 The Parties are independent contractors. Nothing creates a partnership, joint venture, fiduciary relationship, franchise, or agency. Neither Party may bind the other. Vendor is solely responsible for compensation, direction, and taxes of its personnel.

30.2 Neither Party's failure or delay in exercising a right waives it. A waiver must be written and signed by an authorized representative and applies only to the stated instance. Remedies are cumulative unless an exclusive remedy is expressly identified.

30.3 If a court finds a provision unenforceable, it will be modified to the minimum extent needed to make it enforceable while preserving intent, and the remainder continues. Headings aid reference only. “Including” means “including without limitation,” and “or” is inclusive.

30.4 This Agreement, its exhibits, and executed Order Forms are the entire agreement about their subject and supersede prior proposals, statements, and agreements. An amendment must be in a writing signed by authorized representatives of both Parties and expressly identify this Agreement.

30.5 No person other than a Party, a Customer Affiliate ordering Services, a permitted successor, or an indemnified party has a right to enforce this Agreement. The Parties may amend or terminate it without another person's consent, subject to vested indemnity rights.

30.6 This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, each treated as an original, and by electronic signature. An electronic copy is effective as an original. Each signatory represents that they are authorized to bind the named Party.

30.7 Vendor shall not use an artificial-intelligence system to make a legally binding decision for Customer or submit Customer Confidential Information to a third-party model unless an Order Form expressly authorizes that use and specifies safeguards. Vendor remains responsible for output used in providing the Services.
30.8 The Parties have caused their authorized representatives to execute this Agreement as of the Effective Date.

ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.

Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binds Customer anywhere in the Agreement: searches for "solicit", "induce", "recruit", "hire", "employ" and full review of § 12 (Customer Responsibilities), § 16 (Confidentiality) and § 30 (General) return no such restriction, and there is no restricted-period language (no "twelve (12) months" or "directly or indirectly" covenant). **Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 8 already delivers our preferred renewal position:

- **Renewal term (§ 8.2):** successive **twelve-month** periods — no automatic multi-year renewal (walk-away parameter not triggered).
- **Non-renewal notice (§ 8.2):** **30 days'** written notice, exercisable by Customer only — well inside the ≤30-day preferred window, and Vendor has no reciprocal right to force non-renewal.
- **Reminder (§ 8.2):** Vendor must remind Customer **60 days** before renewal, and failure to do so extends our opt-out deadline to 30 days after the reminder is received — a bonus protection beyond the playbook ask.
- **Price uplift (§ 8.3):** capped at the **lesser of CPI and 3%**, with 90 days' notice and no increase applied to prepaid periods.

One note outside this rule's scope: the three-year commitment in § 8.1 is an *initial* term rather than a renewal, so it does not implicate the multi-year auto-renewal walk-away. Separately, § 7.7 (15% of annual Fees per week as liquidated damages for late payment) is a significant customer-side exposure that should be picked up under the late-payment/interest rule.

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The renewal mechanics meet the preferred position in full: renewal terms are twelve months (no multi-year auto-renewal), Customer alone may opt out on only thirty days' written notice, Vendor must send a reminder sixty days before renewal (with the opt-out deadline extended if it fails to do so), and § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and three percent with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods. The three-year commitment in § 8.1 is an initial term, not an automatic multi-year renewal, so it does not trigger the walk-away parameter. No change required for this rule.

Original paragraphs:
p0035: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
p0036: 8.3 On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.

paragraphs.text: 14. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES

14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.

14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.

14.3 Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.

14.4 No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.
15. CUSTOMER DATA AND PRIVACY

15.1 Vendor shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions, to provide the Services, and as permitted by this Agreement. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data, use it for advertising, combine it with another customer's identifiable data, or train a generally available model on it without Customer's express written consent.

15.2 Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law concerning personal information. If Vendor processes personal information for Customer, the Parties' data-processing addendum is incorporated. Vendor is a processor or service provider and shall assist Customer with data-subject requests, impact assessments, consultations, and regulatory inquiries.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant — no redline needed.**

The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant of any kind (no hits for "solicit", "induce", or "recruit" as a restriction; §§ 12, 16 and 30 are clear). Section 12.3 goes further in our favour, expressly preserving Northwind's right to hire anyone responding to general recruitment and recording that "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment."

That is our preferred playbook position (no non-solicit on Customer), so the fallback (mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to service personnel with advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs) is only relevant if Brightline later asks to add one.

paragraphs.text: 13. ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE

13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.

13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.

13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.

13.4 Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline needed.

Section 28 lands squarely on our preferred GOVLAW position:

- **§ 28.1 — Governing law:** Laws of the State of New York, conflict-of-law principles excluded, CISG disclaimed.
- **§ 28.2 — Forum:** Exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County, New York, with mutual submission to personal jurisdiction and waiver of venue/inconvenient-forum objections.
- **Arbitration:** A document-wide search for "arbitration" returned zero hits, so there is no foreign seat or mandatory arbitration overriding the court forum — notable given the counterparty is a UK Ltd., where a non-approved law or London/offshore seat was the plausible risk flagged by the planner.

Two ancillary provisions were reviewed and raise no issue because they are mutual and narrow:

- The § 28.2 carve-out permitting either Party to seek **temporary** injunctive relief in another competent court is limited to confidential information and IP protection — this benefits us as much as the Vendor.
- The § 28.3 pre-filing executive escalation (15 business days) expressly **does not** delay urgent relief or a filing needed to preserve a limitations period, so it cannot be used to stall our claims.

No jurisdiction or venue language elsewhere in the agreement competes with Section 28.

Rule:
ID: GOVLAW
Title: Governing law and venue
Kind: parametric
Summary: Accepted laws are New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales; courts, not foreign arbitration.
Severity: medium
Category: governing-law
Position — preferred:
Laws of the State of New York; exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County.
Position — fallback:
Delaware or California law and courts; or the laws of England and Wales with the courts of London.
Position — walk-away:
Vendor's home jurisdiction outside the accepted list with exclusive foreign venue, or mandatory arbitration seated abroad.
Detection guidance:
Find the governing-law clause; extract jurisdiction and dispute forum; note any arbitration seat.
Redline guidance:
Replace only the jurisdiction words and forum; keep the rest of the sentence intact.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 28 matches our preferred position exactly: § 28.1 selects the laws of the State of New York (with CISG disclaimed), and § 28.2 gives the state and federal courts in New York County, New York exclusive jurisdiction, with mutual submission to personal jurisdiction and waiver of venue/forum objections. A document-wide search returned no arbitration provision, so there is no offshore arbitration seat or competing foreign venue despite the counterparty being a UK Ltd. The § 28.2 carve-out for temporary injunctive relief in another competent court and the § 28.3 pre-filing executive escalation are mutual, standard, and expressly do not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings, so neither disadvantages us. No redline required.

p0115: 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.
p0116: 28.2 The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.
p0117: 28.3 Before filing an ordinary commercial claim, a Party shall give notice and permit executives with settlement authority to meet in good faith within fifteen business days. This process does not delay urgent relief or a filing needed to preserve a limitations period. Discussions are compromise negotiations to the extent allowed by law.

Confidential Information: 16.1 “Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.

content.text:
My investigation is complete. The termination architecture fully meets our preferred position:

- **§ 9.4** gives Customer an unrestricted convenience right ("without cause") over the Agreement or any Order Form, with only accrued Fees owed and a refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (pro-rata refund).
- **§ 29.4** sets that notice period at exactly thirty days — matching our preferred 30 days, so the cross-reference resolves favourably rather than hiding a longer period.
- **§ 10.2** reinforces the prepaid-fee refund on termination.
- **No early-termination fee or penalty** exists anywhere (§ 7 contains no termination charge; § 7.6 blocks unidentified charges; the only liquidated-damages clause in § 7.7 relates to late invoice payment, which is outside this rule's scope).
- **Vendor has no convenience right.** Its only termination rights are mutual: material breach (§ 9.1) and insolvency (§ 9.2). Searches for "Vendor may terminate", "convenience", and "without cause" return no Vendor discretionary exit, and § 20.5 (p0087) and § 24.4 (p0102) affirmatively restrain Vendor from terminating unaffected Services or terminating on Customer change of control.

Since the clause already achieves the preferred position, no redline is warranted.

input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
input.rationale: Meets the preferred position in full. Section 9.4 grants Customer a convenience ("without cause") termination right over the Agreement or any individual Order Form, limits Customer's exposure to accrued Fees only, and requires Vendor to refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (a pro-rata refund, reinforced by Section 10.2). The notice period is supplied by cross-reference to Section 29.4, which resolves to thirty days before the effective termination date — exactly the preferred 30 days. No early-termination fee, penalty, or acceleration attaches: searches for "early termination", "penalty", and "remainder of the term" surface nothing applicable, and Section 7.6 bars charges not identified in the Order Form (the Section 7.7 liquidated-damages provision is a late-invoice-payment matter outside this rule). On direction, Vendor has no convenience right during the three-year term (Section 8.1): its only termination rights are the mutual ones for uncured material breach (Section 9.1) and insolvency (Section 9.2), and searches for "Vendor may terminate", "convenience", and "without cause" return no Vendor discretionary exit. Sections 20.5 and 24.4 further restrain Vendor from terminating unaffected Services or terminating on a Customer change of control. No redline needed.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

content.text:
My investigation is complete. The termination architecture fully meets our preferred position:

- **§ 9.4** gives Customer an unrestricted convenience right ("without cause") over the Agreement or any Order Form, with only accrued Fees owed and a refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (pro-rata refund).
- **§ 29.4** sets that notice period at exactly thirty days — matching our preferred 30 days, so the cross-reference resolves favourably rather than hiding a longer period.
- **§ 10.2** reinforces the prepaid-fee refund on termination.
- **No early-termination fee or penalty** exists anywhere (§ 7 contains no termination charge; § 7.6 blocks unidentified charges; the only liquidated-damages clause in § 7.7 relates to late invoice payment, which is outside this rule's scope).
- **Vendor has no convenience right.** Its only termination rights are mutual: material breach (§ 9.1) and insolvency (§ 9.2). Searches for "Vendor may terminate", "convenience", and "without cause" return no Vendor discretionary exit, and § 20.5 (p0087) and § 24.4 (p0102) affirmatively restrain Vendor from terminating unaffected Services or terminating on Customer change of control.

Since the clause already achieves the preferred position, no redline is warranted.

input.rationale: Meets the preferred position in full. Section 9.4 grants Customer a convenience ("without cause") termination right over the Agreement or any individual Order Form, limits Customer's exposure to accrued Fees only, and requires Vendor to refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (a pro-rata refund, reinforced by Section 10.2). The notice period is supplied by cross-reference to Section 29.4, which resolves to thirty days before the effective termination date — exactly the preferred 30 days. No early-termination fee, penalty, or acceleration attaches: searches for "early termination", "penalty", and "remainder of the term" surface nothing applicable, and Section 7.6 bars charges not identified in the Order Form (the Section 7.7 liquidated-damages provision is a late-invoice-payment matter outside this rule). On direction, Vendor has no convenience right during the three-year term (Section 8.1): its only termination rights are the mutual ones for uncured material breach (Section 9.1) and insolvency (Section 9.2), and searches for "Vendor may terminate", "convenience", and "without cause" return no Vendor discretionary exit. Sections 20.5 and 24.4 further restrain Vendor from terminating unaffected Services or terminating on a Customer change of control. No redline needed.

Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

paragraphs.text: 24. ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL

24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.

24.2 Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld for an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.

24.3 For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.

24.4 Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall cooperate with reasonable administrative changes needed to reflect a permitted successor.
4. ORDER FORMS AND AFFILIATE ORDERS

4.1 An Order Form becomes binding when signed by both Parties. Changes in scope, assumptions, quantities, Fees, dependencies, or dates require a written change order signed by authorized representatives. Vendor shall not charge for work outside scope that Customer did not approve in a signed change order.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 24 (Assignment and Change of Control) already delivers our preferred position on all four elements:

- **24.1** — Customer may assign without Vendor consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets (prompt notice + assignee assumption, which is acceptable).
- **24.2** — Vendor may not assign, delegate material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld for a capable, financially sound assignee), and never to a direct Customer competitor.
- **24.3** — Residual assignments are governed by a mutual, reasonableness-qualified consent standard.
- **24.4** — Expressly negates any Vendor right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on our change of control, and requires Vendor cooperation with successor administrative changes.

I also checked for residual or conflicting language: a document-wide search for "assign" and "change of control" surfaced nothing adverse. Section 9 termination is limited to insolvency-type events (no change-of-control trigger), Section 13 confirms our licence rights transfer with a Section 24-permitted assignment, and Section 30.5 preserves enforcement rights for permitted successors and Customer Affiliates. Walk-away risks (blanket bar on our assignment, or a Vendor exit/re-pricing right on our change of control) are absent.

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 24 already matches our preferred position: 24.1 gives Customer a consent-free right to assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor; 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our consent (reasonableness-qualified) and never to a direct Customer competitor; 24.3 applies a mutual reasonable-consent standard to other assignments; and 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on Customer's change of control. A document-wide search for "assign" and "change of control" found no residual assignment restriction or change-of-control trigger elsewhere (Section 9 termination is limited to insolvency events; Section 13.x and 30.5 reinforce successor/Affiliate rights). No redline needed.

Original paragraphs:
p0099: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.
p0100: 24.2 Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld for an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.
p0101: 24.3 For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.
p0102: 24.4 Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall cooperate with reasonable administrative changes needed to reflect a permitted successor.

paragraphs.text: 22. AUDIT RIGHTS

22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.

22.2 Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.

22.3 Audit findings are Customer Confidential Information and may be used only to enforce this Agreement. Vendor shall provide a copy of the final report. Payment of a shortfall resolves the audited quantity issue absent fraud or demonstrable error.
23. RECORDS AND CUSTOMER ASSURANCE

paragraphs.text: 14. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES

14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.

14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.

14.3 Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.

14.4 No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.

Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

input.rationale: Absence confirmed by exhaustive search: no hits for "solicit", "induce", "recruit" (other than § 12.3's carve-out), "poach", or any restricted-period language ("twelve (12) months", "directly or indirectly" covenant), and the only affirmative "Customer shall not" obligation in the Agreement is § 13.4 (reverse engineering). Full reads of § 12 (Customer Responsibilities), § 16 (Confidentiality) and § 30 (General) — the sections where a non-solicit would sit — contain none. Accordingly no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binds Northwind, which is our preferred position ("no non-solicit on Customer"), and no redline or counterparty comment is proposed. Section 12.3 independently supports the finding: it preserves Customer's freedom to hire "any person who responds to general recruitment" — the substantive equivalent of a general-solicitation/general-advertising carve-out — and records that Customer has made no no-hire commitment. The deterministic checks for a ≤ 12-month duration and a general-solicitation carve-out are heuristics keyed to an existing non-solicit covenant; with no covenant binding Customer they have nothing to measure and do not undercut compliance. Our fallback (mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire) would only be engaged if Vendor later proposes adding such a clause.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.

"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Section 12.3 independently supports the finding: it preserves Customer's freedom to hire "any person who responds to general recruitment" — the substantive equivalent of a general-solicitation/general-advertising carve-out — and records that Customer has made no no-hire commitment. The deterministic checks for a ≤ 12-month duration and a general-solicitation carve-out are heuristics keyed to an existing non-solicit covenant; with no covenant binding Customer they have nothing to measure and do not undercut compliance. Our fallback (mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire) would only be engaged if Vendor later proposes adding such a clause.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 9 already delivers our preferred T4C position on both halves of the rule:

| Requirement | Preferred position | Document |
|---|---|---|
| Customer convenience right | Yes | § 9.4 — "without cause", Agreement or any Order Form |
| Notice period | 30 days | § 29.4 — thirty days |
| Prepaid fee refund | Pro-rata | § 9.4 + § 10.2 |
| Early-termination fee | None | None present |
| Vendor convenience right | None mid-term | None — breach/insolvency only |

The one point worth flagging as a drafting observation (not a deviation): the notice period in § 9.4 is not stated inline but buried as a cross-reference into the *Notices* section (§ 29.4). It happens to resolve to thirty days, so the substance is correct, but that placement is unusual and easy to lose in later amendment rounds. If the negotiation reopens Section 9 or 29 for any other reason, it would be worth folding "thirty (30) days'" directly into § 9.4 as housekeeping — though it does not justify spending a redline on its own.

Two items surfaced during the sweep that fall outside this rule and should be picked up by their own playbook rules if not already covered:

- **§ 7.7** imposes liquidated damages of *fifteen percent of annual Fees per week* an invoice remains unpaid, starting ten days after the due date. This is a late-payment provision rather than a termination penalty, so it is not a T4C deviation — but it is an extremely aggressive one-way charge against us and almost certainly a high-severity issue under the fees/late-payment rule.
- **§ 8.1** sets a three-year term with **§ 8.2** auto-renewing Order Forms in twelve-month increments; the auto-renewal mechanics are Customer-favourable here (thirty days' notice plus a reminder obligation), but they belong to the term/renewal rule.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Meets the preferred position in full. Section 9.4 grants Customer a convenience ("without cause") termination right over the Agreement or any individual Order Form, limits Customer's exposure to accrued Fees only, and requires Vendor to refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (a pro-rata refund, reinforced by Section 10.2). The notice period is supplied by cross-reference to Section 29.4, which resolves to thirty days before the effective termination date — exactly the preferred 30 days. No early-termination fee, penalty, or acceleration attaches: searches for "early termination", "penalty", and "remainder of the term" surface nothing applicable, and Section 7.6 bars charges not identified in the Order Form (the Section 7.7 liquidated-damages provision is a late-invoice-payment matter outside this rule). On direction, Vendor has no convenience right during the three-year term (Section 8.1): its only termination rights are the mutual ones for uncured material breach (Section 9.1) and insolvency (Section 9.2), and searches for "Vendor may terminate", "convenience", and "without cause" return no Vendor discretionary exit. Sections 20.5 and 24.4 further restrain Vendor from terminating unaffected Services or terminating on a Customer change of control. No redline needed.

Original paragraphs:
p0041: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
p0122: 29.4 The notice period referenced in Section 9.4 is thirty days before the effective termination date and may be given by the methods in Section 29.1.
p0038: 9.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.
p0039: 9.2 Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.
p0045: 10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.

Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.

Order Form: 1.7 “Order Form” means a written ordering document signed by authorized representatives of both Parties that references this Agreement and describes the Services, Deliverables, subscription quantities, service levels, Fees, and term purchased by Customer. A purchase order is an administrative convenience only and does not amend an Order Form or this Agreement.

paragraphs.text: 7. FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.

7.2 Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

7.3 Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

7.4 Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

7.5 Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.
7.6 Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.

7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
21. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.

21.2 Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill, to the extent those damages are legally excludable. Costs of restoring Customer Data, obtaining replacement services, required notices, and reasonable incident response are direct damages.

21.3 “Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.

21.4 The limitations allocate risk between sophisticated Parties and apply only to the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law. Nothing limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline needed.

The document already meets our preferred IP position across §§ 13–15:

- **Customer Data / Customer IP (14.1):** Customer owns Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and independently developed IP; Vendor gets only a limited processing right to provide, secure, support and improve the Services *for Customer* — no assignment to Vendor.
- **Deliverables (14.2):** Customer owns each Deliverable on creation, with an express Vendor assignment, matching personnel assignments, and further-assurance covenant.
- **Vendor IP + licence-back (14.3 / 13.2):** Vendor retains only Vendor Technology (defined at 1.9 as pre-existing material, expressly excluding Customer Data and Customer-owned IP), and embedded Vendor Technology carries the § 13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify, create derivative works and permit contractors to support it — exceeding our fallback.
- **No joint ownership (14.4):** Joint IP only by separate signed instrument identifying exploitation rights; feedback is voluntary and Customer retains unrestricted use of its own feedback.

I also checked for the usual leakage points — no aggregated/de-identified data carve-out, no model-training right (15.1 prohibits it absent consent), and § 10 preserves accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences and Customer Data on termination.
